# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `bun run config:docs` from packages/core/src/config/declarations.ts. Do not edit by hand: `bun run check` fails when this file is out of date. -->

Every environment variable Lictory's runtime code reads. The API, the worker
and the migration runner check their variables when they start and stop with
every problem listed at once; tests fail when code reads a variable that is
not declared. Empty or whitespace-only values count as unset, so a deployment
that forwards every variable still gets the defaults.

Where to set them: [`.env.example`](../../.env.example) for local development,
[`deploy/env/production.env.example`](../../deploy/env/production.env.example)
and [`deploy/compose.production.yaml`](../../deploy/compose.production.yaml) for
a server (Compose maps a few names: `ZERO_API_KEY` becomes both Zero keys,
`APP_HOST` becomes `PLATFORM_URL`). Deployment-only settings (hosts, database
passwords, backups, sizing) are described in those files and in
[deployment](./deployment.md); zero-cache's own `ZERO_*` settings follow
[Rocicorp Zero's documentation](https://zero.rocicorp.dev/docs).

## Production rules

With `NODE_ENV=production` (set by the production images):

- Variables marked _In production_ are required.
- A secret must not be a placeholder from an example file or runbook (for
  example `.env.example`'s `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` value, or `generate` left over
  from `deploy/env/*.env.example`).
- Generated secrets need at least 32 bytes. Use `openssl rand -hex 32`.
- Outside production the same checks for missing required values, whole
  numbers, origins and choices apply; secrets are not checked.

Development fallbacks (`BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `localhost` origins) apply only
outside production.

## Delivery credentials key

`DELIVERY_CREDENTIALS_KEY` encrypts stored Jira API tokens. Without it the key
is derived from `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, which ties rotating one to the other.

- **New installations** must set it before connecting Jira. In production,
  connecting Jira is refused while the key is unset and no delivery
  credentials are stored yet (no `delivery_connection` row exists, including
  archived ones). The rest of Lictory works without it.
- **Existing installations** that already stored credentials with the derived
  key keep working unchanged. The API and the worker log a `config.warning` at
  startup. To decouple the two secrets without re-entering tokens, set
  `DELIVERY_CREDENTIALS_KEY` to the current `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` value (it
  derives the same key); `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` can then rotate on its own.
- Never rotate `DELIVERY_CREDENTIALS_KEY` once credentials are stored: they
  become unreadable and every Jira connection must be reconnected.

## Services

| Service             | What it is                                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| api                 | HTTP API (`apps/api`)                                                                       |
| worker              | Background worker (`apps/worker`)                                                           |
| migrate             | Migration runner (`bun run db:migrate`, the `migrate` image)                                |
| platform            | Platform SPA build and Vite dev server (`apps/platform`); values are embedded at build time |
| website             | Marketing website (`apps/marketing`); most values are embedded at build time                |
| edge-proxy          | Local single-origin proxy for development and browser tests (`scripts/edge-proxy.ts`)       |
| rebuild-projections | Operator script that rebuilds read projections (`scripts/rebuild-projections.ts`)           |

## Runtime

| Variable                | Required | Default                                | Read by                        | Secret | Description                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NODE_ENV`              | No       | `development`                          | api, worker, platform, website | No     | `production` turns on the production rules: required settings, placeholder and length checks for secrets, no development fallbacks. Production images set it. |
| `PORT`                  | No       | `3002` (API), `3120` (Vite dev server) | api, platform                  | No     | Port the API, or the platform's Vite dev server, listens on.                                                                                                  |
| `HOST`                  | No       | `0.0.0.0`                              | api                            | No     | Interface the API listens on.                                                                                                                                 |
| `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS`   | No       | `25000`                                | api                            | No     | How long the API drains requests after SIGTERM before it stops.                                                                                               |
| `PLATFORM_DIST_DIR`     | No       | `apps/platform/dist`                   | api, edge-proxy                | No     | Directory of the built platform SPA; the API serves its `index.html` as the document.                                                                         |
| `ZERO_SERVER_LOG_LEVEL` | No       | `error`                                | api                            | No     | Log level of the API's Zero query and mutate handlers. Domain rejections are logged at `warn`.                                                                |

## Database

| Variable                | Required          | Default        | Read by                                   | Secret | Description                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | ----------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_URL`          | Yes (api, worker) |                | api, worker, migrate, rebuild-projections | Yes    | PostgreSQL connection of the application role. The migration runner uses it only for the `local` target. |
| `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` | No                | `DATABASE_URL` | api, worker, migrate, rebuild-projections | Yes    | Direct connection (never a transaction pooler) for LISTEN/NOTIFY when `DATABASE_URL` is pooled.          |

## Database migrations

| Variable                               | Required | Default | Read by | Secret | Description                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_MIGRATION_TARGET`            | No       | `local` | migrate | No     | Which environment the migration runner may change. See docs/operations/migrations.md.                                       |
| `DATABASE_MIGRATION_TRANSPORT`         | No       | `tls`   | migrate | No     | How a remote target is reached: TLS, or the single-server Compose network.                                                  |
| `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL`               | No       |         | migrate | Yes    | Owner-role connection for migrations; required for every remote target.                                                     |
| `DATABASE_MIGRATION_EXPECTED_HOST`     | No       |         | migrate | No     | Host `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` must match for remote targets, so a swapped secret cannot migrate the wrong database.         |
| `DATABASE_MIGRATION_EXPECTED_DATABASE` | No       |         | migrate | No     | Database name `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` must match; required for the `compose-internal` transport.                           |
| `LICTORY_ENVIRONMENT`                  | No       |         | migrate | No     | Name of the environment the stack runs (`production`, `staging`); confirms the target for the `compose-internal` transport. |
| `MIGRATION_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`          | No       | `300`   | migrate | No     | How long to wait for another migration run's lock before giving up.                                                         |
| `MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT`               | No       | `10s`   | migrate | No     | PostgreSQL `lock_timeout` while migrating.                                                                                  |
| `MIGRATION_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT`          | No       | `10min` | migrate | No     | PostgreSQL `statement_timeout` while migrating.                                                                             |

## Authentication

| Variable                      | Required            | Default  | Read by     | Secret          | Description                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------- | -------- | ----------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`          | In production (api) |          | api, worker | Yes, ≥ 32 bytes | Signs sessions and auth tokens. Rotating it signs everyone out. Keep it separate per environment. Also derives the delivery credentials key when `DELIVERY_CREDENTIALS_KEY` is unset. |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`            | No                  |          | api         | No              | Google sign-in. The button is active when both the client ID and secret are set.                                                                                                      |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`        | No                  |          | api         | Yes             | Google OAuth client secret.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`         | No                  |          | api         | No              | Microsoft sign-in. The button is active when both the client ID and secret are set.                                                                                                   |
| `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`     | No                  |          | api         | Yes             | Microsoft Entra client secret.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID`         | No                  | `common` | api         | No              | Entra tenant that may sign in.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `OAUTH_PROXY_URL`             | No                  |          | api         | No              | HTTPS origin of the OAuth callback server for local and preview deployments. Set together with `OAUTH_PROXY_SECRET`. See docs/operations/oauth-proxy.md.                              |
| `OAUTH_PROXY_SECRET`          | No                  |          | api         | Yes, ≥ 32 bytes | Secret shared by the OAuth proxy and its participants (at least 32 characters).                                                                                                       |
| `OAUTH_PROXY_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` | No                  |          | api         | No              | Comma-separated origins the OAuth callback server returns to. Exact origins or a narrow pattern, never a whole hosting domain.                                                        |

## Email

| Variable            | Required | Default                                                                                       | Read by     | Secret | Description                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`    | No       |                                                                                               | api, worker | Yes    | Sends email through Resend. When unset, email goes to the SMTP server below. Production needs Resend or `SMTP_HOST`. See docs/operations/deployment.md#email. |
| `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` | No       | `Lictory <no-reply@email.lictory.com>` outside production; required in production with Resend | api, worker | No     | Sender address for Resend, on a domain verified in Resend.                                                                                                    |
| `SMTP_HOST`         | No       | `localhost` (Mailpit) outside production                                                      | api, worker | No     | SMTP server used when `RESEND_API_KEY` is unset; required in production without Resend.                                                                       |
| `SMTP_PORT`         | No       | `587` in production, `1025` (Mailpit) otherwise                                               | api, worker | No     | SMTP port: 587 for submission with STARTTLS, 465 for TLS from the first byte, 25 for a relay.                                                                 |
| `SMTP_SECURE`       | No       | `true` on port 465, else `false`                                                              | api, worker | No     | TLS from the first byte (SMTPS).                                                                                                                              |
| `SMTP_REQUIRE_TLS`  | No       | `false`                                                                                       | api, worker | No     | Refuse to send unless STARTTLS succeeds; recommended for any server reached over the internet.                                                                |
| `SMTP_USER`         | No       |                                                                                               | api, worker | No     | SMTP user; authentication is used when user and password are set.                                                                                             |
| `SMTP_PASSWORD`     | No       |                                                                                               | api, worker | Yes    | SMTP password, used verbatim.                                                                                                                                 |
| `SMTP_FROM`         | No       | `Lictory <no-reply@lictory.local>` outside production; required in production with SMTP       | api, worker | No     | Sender address for SMTP.                                                                                                                                      |
